item.text:
## 1. Make a small “Tide Lines” educational table display

Use Mara’s captions and water-level observations to make a simple display about how changing water levels affect familiar paths. The archive includes three dated observations and two caption drafts; Mara’s permission covers reuse of her written notes and captions in free public educational displays ([observations.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/observations.txt), [text-fragments.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/text-fragments.txt), [tide-notes.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/tide-notes.txt)). A small free library table display may be possible next month, pending staff confirmation ([venue.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/venue.txt)).

**Next steps:** Confirm the date with library staff. Check whether the shared printer is available and whether the shelf supplies are still there. Draft a few black-and-white pages using only Mara’s text and observations; keep within the $30 cap. The archive lists an $8 quote for up to twelve pages, expiring next month ([printing-quote.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/printing-quote.txt), [printing.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/printing.txt), [craft-box.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt), [request.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/request.txt)).

**Uncertainties:** The table is not booked. The observation log is explicitly not a scientific dataset, so present it as personal field notes. Verify the 1981 historical claim against its original reference before using it ([research.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/research.txt)). Do not use the indexed photos without the photographer’s separate written consent; none is recorded. The recording mentioned in the archive is absent, and its public-use permission is unconfirmed ([photo-terms.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/photo-terms.txt), [sound-index.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/sound-index.txt), [sound-terms.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/sound-terms.txt)).

## 2. Make a hands-on “Folded Water” paper demonstration

A small demonstration could use folded card and blue paper bands to show how one repeated shape represents a changing shoreline. The workshop notes describe moving paper cutouts and the materials list says a prototype used white card, blue offcuts, and scissors ([workshop.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/workshop.txt), [demo-notes.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/demo-notes.txt), [materials.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/materials.txt)). The shelf inventory lists similar supplies, though it should be checked before production ([craft-box.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt)).

**Next steps:** If the supplies are still available, make a simple paper demonstration during Mara’s free weekend time. Use the workshop’s three-slit description as a guide, and keep the activity small and free. The archive gives a three-slit pattern description but no finished stencil ([shape-diagram.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/shape-diagram.txt)); the earlier copy says two slits, so the pattern details need resolving before making a public-facing version ([old-copy.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/old-copy.txt)).

**Uncertainties and restriction:** The maker agreement says pattern FW-7 cannot be publicly displayed or adapted without separate written permission, which has not been granted in the record ([folded-water.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/folded-water.txt)). So this is only a viable public proposal if that permission is obtained first. The motorized lightbox in the old plan was never ordered, and a projector is unavailable ([old-plan.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/old-plan.txt), [other-materials.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/other-materials.txt)).

These two concepts are the strongest archive-based options. The other notes are either unrelated or do not establish current materials or permissions, so they do not support a similarly practical proposal.
